chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one in Ihram, to whom a beautiful woman of good constitution is described, and he discharges (semen), he said: There is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The one in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who ejaculates due to hearing a description of a woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes that merely hearing a description of a beautiful woman while in Ihram, which leads to ejaculation, does not incur the penalty of *dam* (sacrifice) because the cause is external auditory stimulation rather than direct visual or tactile contact. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between involuntary physiological responses triggered by external stimuli and deliberate acts that break the sanctity of the pilgrimage state. It underscores the principle of ease (*yusr*) in ritual obligations when the individual's intent remains pure despite the physical outcome.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Sama’at,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the one in Ihraam to whom the beautiful woman describes her creation, so he discharges. Heasws said: ‘There is nothing upon her’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram, a beautiful woman describes her beauty and he discharges semen. He (the Imam) said, ‘There is nothing on him.’”
